- Units recorded in the form: 7 of 7 files. Conflicts with the column-name hint: none. Scale not stated in the form: none.
- The model uses 12-month log growth for exports, imports and both lending series, so a constant unit scale (thousand vs million) cancels out of the model inputs; the currency does not, because the growth of a USD or KZT value includes exchange-rate and price movements.

## Consumption series (`consumption_history_updated.csv`)

### (a) Frequency and date range of the CSV

- Column `consumption_yoy`; 140 rows from 2015-01 to 2026-08; missing months 0; duplicate months 0.
- Frequency: monthly, every calendar month present.
- Month-to-month repeats: 4 of 139 consecutive pairs are equal; the longest run of one identical value is 2 months.
- Form (student statement): Monthly series; the CSV holds the year-on-year percentage change, which the student checked against the source. Derived by manual cleaning from the downloaded Excel file (student statement). Upper bound from file update date: 37 days; true release lag UNKNOWN. Observation only, not a lag rule: the retail-trade February 2025 issue was published 2025-03-12 (12 days after the month ended).

### (b) How the values reach the decision dates

- `src/ingest.py` reads the file with `read_monthly_series`, keeps the values as levels (consumption is not in `LOG_GROWTH_FEATURES`), reindexes to calendar months with `complete_month_calendar` and selects one month per decision with `apply_release_lag` → `align_to_decision_months`.
- `complete_month_calendar` leaves a missing month as missing; `align_to_decision_months` looks up exactly one reference month. Fill or interpolation calls found in `src/ingest.py`: none. **No interpolation and no forward or backward fill** is applied in the ingest path.
- Check against the data: for all 88 usable decisions in `data/processed/model_panel.csv`, the consumption value equals the raw CSV value at the reference month (mismatches: 0).
- Reuse of one value: in 2 reference months, two or more decisions fall in the same calendar month and therefore use the same consumption value (4 decisions in total). This is a repeated lookup, not an interpolation.

### (c) Release-lag rule

- Each decision uses the value for the calendar month 2 months before the decision month (`assumed_release_lag_months` in `config/release_lag.json`), the same rule as for every factor.
- Real publication lag from the form: UNKNOWN. Whether the assumption holds is reported in `outputs/release_lag_check.md`.
- Source (form): publisher Bureau of National Statistics; URL https://stat.gov.kz/api/iblock/element/4084/file/ru/; retrieved 2026-10-08.
